text:
The first five minutes of FJORD

I understand that it sometimes takes a large number of financiers to get a film into production, especially when you have A-listers like Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve to pay out.

Even still, filmmakers, I beg: if each of the studios are contractually obligated to have a logo at the top, put some music over it, speed it up, do *something* besides letting them play in a never-ending succession, either with awkward silence (bad) or each having their own silly musical sting (worse.)

My audience went from scoffing, to groaning, to outright laughing. Not exactly the vibe you want going into a 2.5 hour family drama. It completely took me out of focus before the first actual frame of the movie. I haven't seen one this egregious since LATE NIGHT WITH THE DEVIL.

EDIT, since some want to read this post in bad faith: the amount of *time* it takes to watch the logos is not my issue (and I see plenty of international films, I'm well aware that having this many studios involved is commonplace.) I am specifically addressing the awkward energy created in the room by presenting the volume of them as individual pieces, rather than cohering.

text:
Is this the writing on the wall?

Today was the third time in a couple months I’ve been to a movie where all of the lights were on after the movie started. 3 different states between California and Texas. Each time one of us had to go seek someone out and it took at least 10 minutes to fix. That’s an issue in and of itself. But! The real issue is the customer service process. It seems to be completely broken at AMC.

If I were to have bought a ticket the “normal” way, I’d get a refund from the manager and likely some kind of voucher(s) for the issue / time wasted.

But for A-listers, we have to rely on opening a ticket with customer service online. It used to be decent, especially when you could message them on Facebook messenger. 

But now? It’s all through a form, no number to call either. And when they say it might take 3 business days to get back, they’re correct. The issue is, I’m not able to “cancel” my movie after it has started. So that’s a wasted ticket until they get back (in a few business days). Having spoken to managers at theaters, the sentiment does also feel like “you have to contact THEM” because theater managers are not “them.” This seems like something AMC could easily fix. Someone at a theater that could make changes to your account…

To me this is part of a broader issue we’ve seen with AMC the past year. They truly have biffed it when it comes to their online ordering being down / inaccessible every time a popular screening gets opened (Odyssey, Spider-Man, Avengers, next Digger?). I’ll never forget waiting 30 minutes in the queue just to get a ticket to “The Invite” since everyone was freaking out about Odyssey. So we know their IT / web people can’t handle a rush. We also know their theater QC seems to be struggling. We also know their customer service support is abysmal. 

What does this tell us about the state of AMC? Is this the writing on the \*screen? All while prices continue to go up…
label: complaint

text:
Bring True 70mm IMAX Film Back To Minnesota

Minnesota Zoo's legendary 70mm IMAX closed in 2019, and we haven't had a true film-projection IMAX since. Meanwhile, smaller metros like Colorado Springs and Rochester just got brand new ones installed. The Twin Cities has 3.7 million people and zero access to the format.

I started a petition asking AMC Theatres and IMAX to install a real 15/70 film system in Minnesota—or at least publicly study whether it makes sense. They already run an IMAX in Rochester, already program 70mm film elsewhere, and are headquartered in Milwaukee. The Heights Theatre in Columbia Heights proves the audience is there: they regularly sell out standard 70mm screenings.

When Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey hit IMAX screens, 70mm showings sold out \\\*weeks\\\* in advance. Dune: Part Three arrives this December in 70mm—and once again, Minnesotans will have to drive six hours to Chicago to see it as the filmmaker intended.

We had one of the great IMAX audiences in the country. This doesn't feel like an impossible ask.

If this resonates with you—if you've felt that loss or want to see Minnesota's cinema culture taken seriously again—consider signing and sharing. Learn more at imaxmn.com.
label: complaint

text:
"The Best Christmas Pageant Ever" A-List pocket Review

Well, I will be unable to see movies from Saturday - Thursday this week, so decided to squeeze in a double-feature Friday, and the first up was "Christmas Pageant". I am a traditionalist, Christmas season starts for me the moment the last turkey breast sandwich is eaten on Thanksgiving evening, but I figured this film might not linger that long, so decided to see it. FYI, this movie is based on a book or story from the 1970s, but I have never read it, and was unfamiliar with it going in.

Anyway, I was glad I did. The movie is about a family of kids, the "Herdmans" I think, who are incorrigible, always causing trouble around town. If they have parental supervision nobody is aware of it, nobody ever sees the parents. For entirely un-Christian motives, the kids bully their way in to the local church Christmas pageant, run by the always good Judy Greer, herself on the outs with the snooty clique that runs the church. This is a tale of redemption and learning, which, because of the good acting by the various kids involved, and the smart dialogue from the screenwriters, is mutual. Both the Herdmans and those they interact with grow as a result, and the Christmas spirit shines through. The film also nicely captures the feel of its time period. 

B ... Above average Christmas movie. Well-executed. Recommended.

text:
Pausing Movies

Did you know they can pause a movie? 

I went to see Ice Cream Man in Westminster, CO yesterday (not a great movie, btw). Five minutes in, these two women walk in.  They're probably drunk and trying to find their seat.  They are talking to each other loudly, trying to hear each other over the movie.  One whips out her phone full on, not even trying to find the light.  Of course, they're sitting right next to me. 

They sit down and continue to talk full volume to one another.  I leaned over and said "Could you please stop talking."  The woman looked at me and said, "Maybe I'll stop if you stop asking." and continued to talk. 

I got up to leave, but there wound up being three ushers in the hall, so I just told them and went back into the movie. Walking back to my seat, the woman pulled out her phone, turned on her camera with flash, took a picture of me and said that I assaulted her. 

Ushers came in once to tell them to stop talking, but they continued to talk.  Another person went out to complain and the ushers came back (maybe with a head usher if that's a thing? He looked older) who told them that they were going to pause the movie and that the women were going to need to leave.  The usher was actually really good at deescalating the situation.  The woman informed him that I had assaulted her, and he just politely said that her money would be refunded and he'd be happy to hear her side of the story outside the theater.  She said she would only leave once the movie was paused. 

They paused it, and the two women made a big showing of slowly getting up, checking to make sure they didn't leave anything and walking out.   People clapped and yelled thank you to the ushers.  It was that bad. 

Anyway, just know that they'll pause the movie for a theater if they need to get rid of someone!  Never seen that before, but I'm glad to know it's an option.

"The Ruse" A-List pocket Review

Well I decided to use A-List slot #2 for the week on a movie called "The Ruse". I admit I didn't know much about this film going in, but it fit an open time slot for me and I was hankering for a movie, so off to my local AMC I went. BTW, I am \*really\* liking the profile photo on the ticket, no more fumbling for my wallet to find my driver's license when an overly conscientious employee wants to see my ID.

But anyway, for a decent  interval of time, I thought I was going to end up recommending "The Ruse". An old woman, confined to bed and living on an oxygen tank, drives off an in-home nurse caregiver, who is replaced by another, a girl named "Dale". The movie has a slow-burn feel to it, as strange things begin to happen in the house. It becomes apparent that the girl Dale replaced has gone missing, and police and detectives and neighbors come sniffing around and the mystery deepens.  And if this sounds kind of dull it really wasn't. The makers do a nice job creating an atmosphere of growing tension. I was kind of drawn in.

Unfortunately, when things do finally come to a head, they do so in  comically inept way. All hell breaks loose, and the explanations for the whys and wherefores strain all credulity. The quality of the film nosedives, and I left the theater shaking my head. Oh well. There's always the Vietnamese film tomorrow.

D+ ... Talk about not sticking the landing, this movie belly-flops. Not recommended.

text:
"Woman In The Yard" A-List pocket Review

Well I like seeing a lot of movies, and I had a free afternoon this past week and this movie fit my schedule. Didn't know much about it though it had the Blumhouse label so I assumed it was a horror film.

Anyway, the movie revolves around a single black mother living with her two kids in a rural farmhouse type home. There was a recent tragedy, the family father was killed in a car accident and the family is trying to recover and make do. A mysterious woman shrouded head to toe in a black veil appears in the yard, and weird things start happening. 

I will say that I liked "TWITY". It is a modest movie, the action centers around what happens at the farmhouse, which makes it easy to follow. The kids and mother do a very good job acting, they convey the creeping weirdness and fear of the situation quite well. That tension comes from without and within, as the evil woman creeps closer, the pressure reveals cracks and hidden secrets among the family members, which adds to the suspense. The makers do a good job building up this atmosphere and tension, which I liked. This is not a wild bloody hack and slash type horror film. The climax is reasonably satisfying, and at just about 80 minutes of run time, it doesn't overstay its welcome.

C+ ... nothing special, but modest creepy movie got the job done. Mildly recommended.

Did anyone go to the 24 hour Best Picture Marathon?

So my husband and I went to that 9 movie Best Picture marathon over the weekend, and that was an experience. I was 100% opposed to it when he first mentioned it to me, but I owed him a celebration for a very special promotion he got and as the day got closer I realized I’d love to re/watch some of these movies so I figured why not.

For those who didn’t go, here are a few noteworthy and cool things:

1. They gave us wristbands to put on to signify that we paid to see to see the marathon and had a security guard there to make sure everyone had one on. They also gave us a little sheet of paper with the schedule on it and it had when each movie started and ended.

2. When they scanned us in, we got a heads up that after 11:30pm we wouldn’t be able to leave the building until 8:30am (since they lock the doors between then). However, they did tell us they were gonna let us on the balcony if we needed fresh air or to take a smoke break and that was cool to go out on the balcony since we never had. Additionally, concessions was open all night with a short break from 12am-1am to give them a chance to clean it up.

3. There were trailers before the first movie…wasn’t expecting that. We didn’t get to see if there was anything after the final movie, but between movies there was a still image on the screen that said “JOIN THE CONVERSATION” with some hashtags to use with “best picture showcase at AMC” or something like that.

4. I brought a blanket and earplugs and slept through Conclave because that was the one I was most uninterested in and then accidentally slept through Dune as well 😔 my husband took a short nap during Dune but holy hell, I can’t imagine staying awake through all 9 of those.

5. My husband and I were very surprised they had I’m Still Here (a subtitled film) second to last…like I would rather them put it earlier instead of after 7 movies. It was right after my nap so I was fine but I felt bad for those who were dedicated enough not to sleep.

6. Every 2-3 movies, the staff would come in with little leftover pins and some posters and ask trivia questions about the nominees where the winners would get a prize. My husband and I didn’t know the answers to any of the questions so we didn’t get any but we were happy for those who won!! (ALSO, the employee was super nice and gave the papers with the trivia questions to my husband when they were done. He was so happy, haha)

7. The people who went there were super cool! We made friends with the girl sitting next to us and the two brothers sitting behind us and talked with them between movies, and we even exchanged Instagrams after.

8. There was a 45 minute “dinner break” at 6:30pm. We got Chipotle for dinner and ran to Target to grab some food for the rest of the night since we wouldn’t be allowed back outside. He was very adamant that we not get anything too fatty/carby to not wear us out, so we mostly got fruit and crackers, haha. We also brought our water bottles that we filled throughout the day/evening/night/morning and that was awesome.

Overall, really cool experience! I wouldn’t be opposed to going again next year but holy fuck I was tired as hell the rest of the day.

Did anyone else go? What was your experience like?

(PS Anora was without a doubt my favorite one 🙂)

EDIT: here was the breakdown of the schedule:

12:00pm - The Brutalist

4:05pm - Nickel Boys

7:10pm - A Complete Unknown

9:40pm - Anora

12:10am The Substance

2:40am - Conclave

4:50am - Dune Part II

7:45am - I’m Still Here

10:10am - Wicked

Since some people are so disturbed I slept during Conclave and Dune I’ll leave some context 🤣

"Ne Zha 2" A-List pocket Review (3D)

Well in addition to this forum, I also participate on a movie box-office forum, although just as a reader mostly, and they have been going crazy the last couple weeks over this movie, a Chinese animation, that apparently has made literally a billion dollars in China alone, and still surging. So when I saw it appear at my local AMC, I just had to find out what all the Chinese fuss was about. Plus, I love foreign animation. And because I also love 3D, I saw it in that format. The movie was presented in a Chinese language, with English subtitles.

Anyway, I admit I quickly lost the plot of "Ne Zha 2". I mean, it was a classic jumbled MCU type plot, at least to my old eyes and ears. And this, even though there was a preamble that recapped I guess what happened in the original movie, this involves some kind of magical pearl that splits into red and blue colors I think.  Set in mythic imperial China of the past, there is a ugly-cute little demon kid, vaunted celestial immortal sages, giant animals such as sharks and turtles wearing armor, three chained dragons living in hell-like molten lava, a nice blue shaded guy who gets killed in battle and whose soul seems to merge into the cute-ugly kid. There is a community called "Shengten Pass" that the cute-ugly wants to protect. There is a short big-headed sage like being, and they all seem to be involved in intrigue and back-stabbing, some literal, that results in angry outbursts of action, some dumb-fun like the first couple Kung-Fu Panda movies, others very serious like an anime movie. Of course there is also an epic world-sweeping, planar mega-battle and the protagonists end up winning, I think. And then there is an extended mid-credits scene, I guess setting up #3. But I was lost from about 10 minutes in, LOL.

What makes "Ne Zha 2" worth seeing anyway is the breathtaking visuals. I have never seen a CGI-animated movie look so crisp and vibrant. This is a bar-setting movie technically, yes, even for Disney/Pixar.  And I \*definitely\* recommend 3D, the 3D presentation is the best  I have ever seen. Crisp and deep and filled with CGI detail. The movie is a visual feast, so I just sat back and absorbed the visuals for the 138 or so minutes.

B ... Complicated "Ultron" type plot with constant chaos eruptions. But a feast to behold.

Maybe someone else will have a better time than I did but this wasn’t worth the time. 1.5/5

SPOILER "Sing Sing" A-List pocket Review

**SPOILER ahead**

Seen at: AMC Southcenter, Seattle

Premise: Colman Domingo is John “Divine G” Whitfield, an incarcerated man at Sing Sing prison, where he participates in a theater program known as Rehabilitation Through the Arts (RTA). He butts heads with and later befriends Clarence “Divine Eye” Maclin (a real life RTA performer playing a version of himself).

Performances: I loved watching the relationship unfold between Domingo and Maclin. Domingo is absolutely fantastic in this role and deserving of the many nods he's gotten so far (and hopefully an Oscar nom this week, too!). The rest of the ensemble cast, mostly RTA alumni playing themselves, are delightful. Sean San José is particularly effective as Mike Mike, Divine G’s cellmate and friend, who is funny, sweet, and heartbreaking.

Writing: Touching without being overly sentimental. A concise story, well-told by its players, that moves along swiftly.

Cinematography: Shot on 16mm, often with natural lighting, and lots of close-ups. Amplified the claustrophobic feeling of incarceration.

Recommended for: Fans of movies about underdogs rising above the expectations placed on them and anyone following the Oscar nominations this year

You might also like to know:

* No violence, but some strong language
* Intense emotions
* >!A main character dies unexpectedly !<\[cw death\]
* The N-word is used briefly
* Staff at the prison are visible but never have any lines

**Overall: A, take your rough-around-the edges family member and have a nice lil cry**

"Wolf Man" A-List pocket Review (IMAX)

Well, my wife for some strange reason liked the "Wolf Man" previews (I never watch previews, just scroll my phone during them), so she decided we would see this movie for our Friday afternoon date day. And because it's A-List, we decided to see it in IMAX.

Anyway, "Wolf Man" doesn't have much going for it. One thing it does is the strangely attractive blonde girl from the "Ozark" TV show. She's quirky-good like she always is. Other than that, it has a decent opening sequence, where the male lead flashbacks to a childhood encounter in the Oregon woods with his dad. The rest is pretty much awful. The man, the Ozark girl, and their kid head up to the same isolated Oregon cabin, and encounter a Wolf Man or two. These wolf men are lame, they lack any fear factor. The woman and child seem to be there solely to be chased around by the Wolf Man, while dad tries to fight them off. This goes on for about 90 minutes, before it mercifully ends.

D ... Just a bad, dull movie. No fear, no frights, just boredom and constant chasing. NOT recommended.

PS - IMAX was strange. The movie had bars top and bottom, but the sound field was pretty awesome. Enveloping and with huge bass. But to a fault: when the lame little Wolf Man would run, the room would shake with massive bass, as if a tyrannosaurus rex was bearing down.

"Venom: The Last Dance" A-List pocket Review (IMAX 3D)

Well I like the big dumb super-hero comic movies, even the Sony-Marvel ones usually, and having seen the first two "Venom" movies, the first being one of my first 25 A-List selections back in 2018 and the second three years later, I had to see Venom 3. And because this is A-List, I saw it in IMAX 3D, easily my favorite movie format (thanks Sony, for releasing it in this format!).

Anyway, my feelings about Venom are mixed. I didn't much care for the first one and was shocked that it was a big hit at the box office. The second one I also didn't like that much either. So I was surprised to find myself liking Venom 3 more than I expected to. I think what got me was I finally bought in to the "buddy movie" aspect of the guy living with Venom symbiont or whatever they call it living in his head. I found myself kind of won over by the interplay between the guy and the Venom thing. Also, for the most part the plot isn't convoluted, and the action set pieces are pretty well done. No, V3 isn't close to being one of the better Marvel movies, but for what it tries to do, it does pretty well.

C+ .... If you've seen the first two, you should see this one too. 

PS - while the film did not fill up the entire IMAX screen, bars were top and bottom, the 3D was well done, deep and crisp, and the sound was very good.

PSS - there is a mid-credit scene and a true end-credit scene.

text:
"It Ends With Us" A-List pocket Review

Well on Friday I wanted to see the new "Alien" movie, but sometimes you have to take one for the marriage, and my wife wanted to see "It Ends With Us", so that is what I ended up seeing. I didn't really know anything about this movie going in, other than my wife said it was based on a popular book.

Anyway, I am not really averse to watching chick-flick type romantic movies, but I found "It Ends With Us" a real slog, the longest 130 or so minutes film I can recall. The clock seemed to drip by agonizingly slowly, like in one of those surreal Dali paintings. The main issue I had was the film largely consists of close-ups of the faces of the  leads, Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni, and occasionally an actor named Brendan Sklenar.  Now these are all good-looking people, but still, just the constant close-ups of their talking heads was just too much for me. I guess this was supposed to convey the emotions, but it just threw me off, kind of like the close-ups of Sean Penn were too much for me in that recent Taxi ride movie. 

The movie itself is about relationships and domestic abuse, and that story is OK. It's pretty people interacting in upscale parts of Boston, so the scenery is nice all around, kind of like "Emily In Paris", but without the latter's light heart and sense of fun. Yeah I know domestic abuse isn't light or fun, but there just wasn't much entertainment value in this movie.

C - minus. Prepare for a long haul. Not really recommended.
label: review

Disclaimer, I have generalized anxiety that's been sort of flaring up lately. I know that's most of what this was. Please don't be rude.

Bright Theaters

I’ve been making it a point to check out different theaters in Chicago to figure out different pros and cons. Sometimes I have to go places with old u comfortable chairs, but the timing is right or it’s near an errand so I deal with it. I decided to get a few tickets to Block 37 in Chicago and I was sooo happy to see that I could go directly from the train station into the mall with the theater… no walking outside in the cold temps!!! It was bright and clean heading into the theater and felt very inviting! That’s where the pros stopped…

It was so bright when Nicole Kidman was on the screen that it looked the way it does before Noovie does at any other theater. The lights dimmed slightly, but it was still distractingly bright. Instead of focusing on ISS, I found myself staring at the wall panels wondering how much they actually dampen the noise. I also kept staring at the ceiling wondering why they still had lights on… each seat has its seat numbers lit up too! At least I was able to read the nutritional facts on my candy clear as day! I even checked to make sure I hadn’t booked the sensory option with bright lights. When I asked staff about it afterward I was told that some movies don’t dim all the way. I went again today to see Iron Claw and it was the exact same thing. To top it all off, both seats were super loud and squeaky when I was utilizing the electric recliners. When I asked staff if there was a way to know which movies dimmed all the way they suggested I try one of the other theaters nearby. 

TLDR: theater bright af and squeaky seats. 

Does anybody else find strange quirks like this? I’m starting to notice they all seem to have their own personality! I cancelled the second movie in my double feature and I’m waiting to see it elsewhere now that’s less distracting. 😂

text:
A True Tale of Dumb Money

I had tickets to see "Dumb Money" with a friend for a 9 PM Thursday night showing at my local AMC. We arrived and took our seats at 9:06 in auditorium 2 as indicated on our tickets. We saw two straight A24 trailers (My first clue that something strange was afoot), and then the previews ended. At that moment, I found it strange that they were only showing 8 minutes of trailers before the movie. My confusion was briefly eased as Nicole Kidman promptly reminded me that heartbreak can feel good in a place like this.

Unfortunately, my confusion returned with a vengeance when it became immediately clear that the movie starting was, in fact, Jonathan Demme's "Stop Making Sense." I like the Talking Heads, and while I considered staying, I decided it was best to figure out what was going on. We left the theater, followed by the stares of fellow moviegoers who were actually in the correct place. We approached the nearest employee, who spent most of the conversation gaslighting us by claiming there had never been a 9 o'clock showing of "Dumb Money." Finally, a manager approached and informed us that due to Taylor Swift and Co's decision to move up the release of the Eras Tour Movie, the entire screen schedule had been changed, and our movie had been canceled.

AMC seemingly did not find it necessary to contact me, aside from an automated "GET EXCITED TO SEE {MOVIE TITLE} IN A FEW HOURS" email. Unfortunately, I was excited to see "Dumb Money," but Taylor Swift got in the way. Apparently, "Dumb Money" is what I gave to AMC, and heartbreak did not feel so good anymore. 

Tl;dr: The Eras Tour movie bumped my screening of Dumb Money and I received no notice.
label: complaint

text:
"Gran Turismo" A-List pocket Review

Well I have never played the "Grand Turismo" video game, I've always preferred the FPS games. But I do think these racing simulator games look awesome, have always wondered what one of those steering wheels cost. So when I saw this film pop up for a Sunday matinee, I decided to see it.

So any way, this movie is linked to the GT game in that sometimes around 10-15 years ago an idea was hatched to try and train some racing simulator game enthusiasts in to actual professional  race car drivers, and this is the story of one guy who did just that - a gamer who became a real racer.

"Gran Turismo" is kind of cheesy. It is high-gloss and melodramatic almost to a fault. But it is also pretty fun. There is great car racing action and SFX, the actor who plays the aspiring driver has charisma, and we get Djimon Hounsou and Orlando Bloom and the hot red head from the Spice Girls as well. Well she's 50 or so now but still. And David Harbour, he's very good as the racing tech mentor for the kid.

Anyway, in the end, I was entertained by GT. It is good summer movie popcorn fare. Like popcorn it is light and empty and maybe not that good for you, but it sure tastes good especially with hot movie theater butter all over it.

C+ ... Escapist fun. Recommended on that basis.

​

text:
"Scoob!" A-List pocket Review

As a kid growing up in the early 1970s, "Scooby Doo" was my favorite Saturday morning TV show. I liked everything about it - it was scary and funny and endearing and we all loved singing the theme song. So I watch movies like this through a mist of nostalgia.

To summarize, "Scoob!" is a mess of a movie, arguably the worst I've seen all year, and I thought "Tom and Jerry", another Warner's animation project, had all but clinched that title three months ago. But this is so bad I need to reevaluate.

For about two minutes early on, when a puppy Scooby meets a child Shaggy, there is a hint of those positive qualities I mention above. Then at about the nine minute mark, they end up at a bowling alley. And bowling pins turn in to crab-like robot monsters. The next 85 or so minutes is cacophony of chaos. The scenes that follow seem like they were positioned by a Random Nonsense Generator, the movie is largely just an assault on the senses. The plot, thin as it is, ends up with the gang - Daphne looks great as always, btw - fighting a three headed ancient Greek mythological dog on some other plane of existence. Yep, that's correct. Or something like that.

Look, at 57 years old, I understand that these movie companies (media entertainment services) are trying to "update" their classic cartoon properties for a new generation of kids who are growing up with Netflix, Iphones and Playstation 6s, or whatever it's up to now. I'm not exactly the target demographic I was a half-century ago. I'm a good five generations of kids out of date here. Still, I'm not  so far behind the times that I can't appreciate a good reboot. I'm a big fan of "Riverdale", the contemporary take on the Archie's comics characters that I also enjoyed back when the Beatles were announcing their breakup and men were first landing on the moon.

But this is no "Riverdale", It's just an ungodly mess, IMHPOV.

text:
"Demon Slayer Mugen Train" A-List pocket Review (IMAX - subtitles)

Well I don't review movies that I don't see via A-List, and up until now this film has famously been excluded. But thanks to a tipoff on this board, I found out today that Demon Slayer has been released to A-List. So I quickly copped a ticket for an IMAX showing, Japanese language with subtitles. I also come to this film as a pure standalone experience, as I have never seen any of the movies or TV shows that the film may be associated with.

In a nutshell, I had a great time watching "Demon Slayer". The film gets off to a slow start, as a motley crew of Demon Slayers are on a train heading who knows where. They kill a couple cool looking demons but then things drift and become surreal, a landscape of dreams, until one Slayer realizes that he's asleep and in a dream, and has to wake up, as he figures a demon has caused this. From this point forward, the movie becomes an action-packed bonanza, as the demon who put everyone to sleep is fought, and then there's an epic battle between a slayer named Regonku, the most advanced of the group, and a "higher level" demon. The animation and special effects are pretty riveting throughout the long battles. There's also a story underlying all this - Regonku's relation to his mother, and another slayer's efforts to come to terms with (I think!) the loss of most of his family, save his sister, at the hands of demons. But the action is what won me over. The film looked and sounded great in the IMAX format.

Highly Recommended, see it in IMAX if you can!

text:
"The Unholy" A-List pocket Review

My third A-List choice this week was "The Unholy", a new horror movie with a religious theme.  Given that we know the basic direction this is heading in due to it being a mishmash of a million other horror films that trace their lineage back to "The Exorcist",  the success or failure of "The Unholy" depends on its execution. 

And basically, I was entertained by its execution. For one thing, the acting is pretty good. The guy who played "Negan" on the Walking Dead is a key participant, as is indie-film cutie Cricket Brown, and we get veterans like Cary Elwes and William Sadler thrown in to the mix as well. They all do fine. I sometimes wonder how actors can avoid cracking a smile when working in films like this, but these professionals take their jobs seriously, LOL.

The main reason I give this film a thumbs-up though is that it passes the  two-prong test of all decent horror films: (1) does it create a foreboding atmosphere that raises tensions throughout, and (b) does it deliver on the big shock moments when they come? The Unholy isn't great in either regard, but it passes both tests, particularly the first one. The director and cinematographer do a nice job of creating a feeling of mild dread that kept me involved.  

So a mild recommendation. If you are looking to fill a third spot on your A-List for the week, this will do pretty nicely.

B-

text:
War (2019) My first foray into Bollywood

Three of the local AMCs in the Seattle area regularly show Independent releases, Foreign films, Documentaries etc. Stuff you would normally have to go to an Arthouse Theater for. Sometimes scheduling is limited but they are almost always included in A-List. 

So last night I went to my first Bollywood film, War. In Hindi with English Subtitles. (IHO Slumdog Millionaire doesn't truly count as Bollywood) Best as I can tell, this movie is a big deal because two top Bollywood stars are in this movie together for the first time ever. Hrithik Roshan and Tiger Shroff are action stars and their movies seem to include wild stunts and chases-then they also sing and dance. It also seems like they have their shirts off as much as possible and their hair is always perfect.

The film was shown in one of the smaller capacity theaters but there were a LOT of people there and probably 90% people of Indian background.(I'm in the other 10%). Here are some general impressions and observations of the movie, with no spoilers.

The movie starts with a nice disclaimer I thought. There was a title card that basically said, this movie is a work of fiction. The filmmakers are not trying to say one group, religion, ethnicity etc. is better than another or inherently evil. We are just trying to tell a story. Have fun and enjoy!

The basic premise of the story is that a special ops soldier in the Indian army, Kabir (played by Roshan) has gone rogue and is killing Indian Government officials. His old team led by his former apprentice, Khalid (played by Shroff) is tasked to eliminate him. The chase for Kabir literally goes all over the world and includes as many big stunts as their budget would allow for.

I felt that I lost some impact due to my unfamiliarity with some of the actors and actresses. There were clearly some big dramatic entrances designed to hype up the audience. There were also some cheesy moments that I was unsure if they were purposely cheesy or unintentional. For example, a truck explodes the camera pans to the fireball in slow motion while Kabir comes into the shot through the fireball riding a motorcycle with big dramatic music. Since discretion is the better part of valor, I suppressed some laughs several times.

Since this is an action movie, I was wondering how the Bollywood dance numbers would be worked in. We got one in the first act. Khalid celebrates his acceptance into Kabir's elite special ops unit by attending a color festival. We got the other late in the second act when "boy meets girl" (Kabir meets his love interest) In general, I like dance numbers so I enjoyed both of them.

I did not realize that it is standard to have an intermission (interval it's called) in Indian movies. I gather in India everyone takes a break, gets snacks etc. At my showing the screen said "Interval" faded to black and then after a few seconds continued with the rest of the movie. At first I was a little confused because the next scene looked like a PSA for good sportsmanship filmed at a kids soccer game but it was actually us getting introduced to a new character (the love interest's young daughter)

Anyway, this movie was loads of fun. Yes it was cheesy and overly dramatic at times but it looked beautiful, had a good classic action movie story, and a lot of really big awesome looking stunts (There is an airplane scene that is just as good if not better than the airplane scene in The Dark Knight Rises). I am definitely doing some research to find other Bollywood movies to watch and keeping current on upcoming releases.
label: review

"Ha-Chan Shake Your Booty!" A-List pocket Review (Japanese)

Well it was a lazy hazy Monday and I decided to see a movie, and since I like to see foreign-language films whenever possible, I decided to see "Ha-Chan", which was presented in the Japanese language, with English subtitles.

Well in one sense, Ha-Chan is a pretty by the numbers chick-flick. A middle aged Japanese woman in Tokyo loves to go ballroom dancing with her husband. When tragedy strikes, she is left emotionally adrift, and her close friends, who fit the usual stereotypes, try to lift her back up. Romance and comedy ensue. But the reason I liked the film was that all of this was executed with good acting, a propulsive story, and comedic aplomb. The main character, played by the always good and fetching Rinko Kikuchi, is engaging and delightful. And the story never comes close to jumping the shark with silliness, as dramedy's often do. I enjoyed this film start to finish, and when the predictable emotional outcomes materialized, they felt well-earned.

B-minus. Light and fun Japanese language dramedy. Recommended.

It Ends A-List pocket Review

What it is: A suspenseful supernatural drama about four friends stuck on a never-ending road who try to find meaning in their suffering. 

Who it's for: Teens transitioning from high school to college, college grads transitioning from college to the work world, tender types who cried reading *The Giver* in grade school, and anyone surviving the unique horrors of the 21st century (endless social media feeds, COVID, climate disasters, etc.). 

Unexpected surprise: I was surprised that this movie really isn't a horror movie. It's more about existential dread than jump scares. There's no gore. And it could be rated PG-13 if they had toned down the cursing. 

Fun fact: This is a tiny film getting in front of big audiences! The budget was just $80,000, and as of this writing, none of the cast have Wikipedia pages.

Overall: This is an extremely divisive movie. I saw it with my best friend who said they hated every minute of it and found it very boring. I had the opposite reaction: I thought it was philosophical, meditative, and pleasantly ambiguous. Go see it with your friends so you can argue about it!

text:
"Hot Spot" A-List pocket Review

Well it was 99 degrees outside so a movie in a cold theater sounded good, and when I read the description of "Hot Spot", a sci-fi movie with apparently a largely Polish production, I decided to see it.

Anyway, I found "Hot Spot" to be, after the first few minutes, largely incomprehensible. The setup was pretty straightforward: In the near future, drought has consumed much of the world, and the lives of the few survivors is managed by "the Head", an AI system that regulates resource usage and much else. Everyone is plugged in to the Head by eating a gummy bear every 24 hours, and if you fail to eat it your head literally explodes. A gruesome murder occurs at one of many refugee camps, and a curly-mullet, 80s jumpsuit wearing detective is sent in to solve it. He encounters Noomi Rapace, who is playing the de facto leader of the refugees, and a reported "cyber witch". 

And then ... what follows is about 80 minutes of seemingly random dreamscapes, chattering between the curly detective and Noomi, an occasional naked woman, and exploding heads. I couldn't make sense of any of it, maybe I am just slow on the uptake, but I couldn't. And then it ends when a large cat appears. That's it.

Still, I was glad I saw "Hot Spot". I left the theater with zero idea about how anything was resolved, but the incomprehensible scenes were stylishly shot and so I enjoyed them as isolated set pieces.

C+ ... Randomly vague and opaque, but a fun watch anyway, at least for me. Mildly recommended for those in the mood for stream of consciousness, or something.

Well I am a sucker for Japanese animation and when I saw that "Your Name" was showing up in the theater for a 10th anniversary screening I decided that I should go see it. Especially since I recall viewing it back in 2016 during its original run and liking it quite a bit. The movie was presented in Japanese with English subtitles, my preferred way to see anime.

Anyway the passage of time has not dimmed my enthusiasm for this film. Two teenagers in modern Japan, a boy and a girl, end up switching bodies somehow. Well it was a lazy hazy hot Tuesday in the deep south, so a trip to the movies seemed like a good idea to us. Problem is, my wife didn't want to see Masters of the Universe or anything like it, so we had to find something else. So there was "Pressure", and since we have both been fans of Brendan Fraser since the 90s, this movie fit the bill.

Anyway, it's early June 1944 in England, and General Eisenhower (Fraser) is under pressure to decide whether to launch the D-Day invasion of France. Problem is, the weather forecast is crucial to the issue, and his personal meteorologist and the British meteorologist can't agree about it. Thus the "pressure" the movie hinges on. 

In one sense, I liked "Pressure". The drama of the real historical moment is self-evident, thus the movie naturally has it in spades. Also, the acting  - particularly by those playing Ike's assistant Kay Sommersby and the English weather man - is very good. The movie movies along crisply and at about 100 minutes doesn't overstay its welcome. But it also has some big problems. One is that this is a rare case where longer would have been better. The events are so important and complex that 100 minutes doesn't seem to do it justice, so there is a "lightweight" feel to the film, it lacks the gravitas of its subject matter. Also and surprisingly, Fraser never captures the look or feel of Eisenhower. His yelling and posturing seems forced and unconvincing. Since he's the pivotal player, that drags thing back a lot.

C+ ... Reasonably entertaining, but recommended for those who devour anything related to WW2 only.

Well there was a time when Guy Ritchie made action movies that had some depth. But IMO it's been a while since he has done so. Nevertheless, because some of his best films are very good, I always hold out hope, so I decided to see "In The Grey" as my first A-List film of the week.

Anyway, like a lot of GR films, "In The Grey" is very slick and fun to look at. The film is basically a James Bond/Mission Impossible type film pitting a shadowy group of underground operatives, led by Jake Gyllenhaal, Henry Cavill, and the very comely Eiza Gonzalez, against a corrupt billionaire who owes their client a billion dollars and refuses to pay. All kinds of transcontinental financial and military skullduggery ensues.

But unfortunately, like a lot of recent GR films, beyond the shiny high-tech glossy people veneer, there isn't really anything going on in this movie. Its 90 minute run time slips by easily enough, and the entertainment value isn't bad, but much of it is implausible and the never-ending action grows tedious. I hope everyone involved got paid well.

C-minus ... glossy generic action thriller. See it if you must. Not really recommended.
label: review

text:
"Meet Me At The Eclipse" A-Lost pocket Review (Vietnam)

Well I was looking for a movie to see on a lazy Wednesday, and as I love seeing foreign-language films when they happen to appear at my local AMC, I decided to see "Meet me at the Eclipse", a new Vietnamese film. The movie was presented in the Vietnamese language, with English subtitles.

Well anyway, in 1989 Vietnam, a beautiful young village woman meets a handsome electrician apprentice and they like each other. Problem is, her strict mother sees this guy as a rakish loser and strongly disapproves, and sets her up to marry the nephew of the local parish priest. Drama ensues from this point forward.

I liked "MMatE" well enough. The film is beautifully shot in Vietnam. There are pretty people and scenery to look at, the acting is good, especially given the somewhat mawkish melodramatic script, which is heavily faux-Shakespeare, star-crossed lovers with doses of comedy and tragedy. The story is also easy to follow and despite its predictability, I was engaged. One historical thing that stood out was the "absence of communism". In 1989 as today, Vietnam was controlled by the communist party, but you'd never know it watching this film. The movie is replete with Catholic imagery, and there is no overt or even subtle communist presence at all. This was curious to me but did not bother me.

C-plus ... sweet, gentle, tragi-comedy-drama. Acting and scenery make up for predictable story. Recommended.
label: review

"Obsession" A-List pocket Review

I saw an Early Access screening of *Obsession* tonight and I think it'll be a hugely popular film this weekend. Take a date! 

**What it is:** A familiar story of a wish granted gone wrong. Bear (Michael Johnston) is in love with his childhood best friend Nikki (Inde Navarrette), but can't bring himself to admit his crush on her, so he makes a wish using an old novelty toy called a One Wish Willow. When his wish is granted, Nikki loves him more than anyone else... and all hell breaks loose. 

**Who it's for**: Fans of *It Follows*, anyone who's ever been in a codependent relationship, people who've experienced the terror of being held hostage by hormonal cycles (their own or someone else's), people who like supernatural stories with funny, modern twists. 

**Unexpected surprise**: Inde Navarrette is incredible in this and the movie wouldn't work at all without her. She abruptly changes tone, contorts every muscle in her face and then holds perfectly still, wails like a child who dropped an ice cream cone on a hot sidewalk, sobs like a sad clown, and slithers along walls in the creepiest fucking ways. 

**Fun fact**: The movie had a budget of $750,000 but feels like it cost way more than that. (Source: [The New Yorker](http://archive.today/v2f2K), 11 May 2026)

**Overall: A+, tense, shocking, creepy, gross, hilarious, fun, disturbing!**

Seen at: AMC Southcenter, Tukwila, WA (Dolby)
label: review

"Marama" A-List pocket Review

Well I like horror movies especially ones that are under an hour and a half,  and since  "Marama" seem to fit both bills I decided to spend an A-List slot on it.

Anyway, it's 1859 in the wilds of Yorkshire, England, and a pretty young woman has traveled to a local estate all the way from the southwest Pacific to learn more about the fate of some family members. She is a Maori woman, a native of New Zealand, which has been colonized by England.

What unfolded over the next 83 minutes was one of the best movies I've seen this year. The estate is gothicly creepy, the British estate owner is a Maori fetishist, and the girl learns awful details about her mother and sister while communing with ancestors. Everything about the movie worked for me. The acting is spot on, the setting is creepy and gloomy, and the makers allow us to feel a slow-burn dread and horror as the secrets of the estate unfold. I was drawn in from the git.

B+ .... right there with Hokum as the year's best horror film so far. Highly endorsed.

text:
Neglected... a mini A-list review (you've been warned)

Listen... I admire when anyone can get a film made. It's tough. So kudos for getting *Neglected* made.

Here are the high or low lights:

* This is one of those blink and you'll miss it, tiny releases. It makes Vertical look like a studio.
* A lot of middle aged white guys that all look alike.
* Josh Duhamel does his best. A cop desperate to solve clues from a serial killer to save his teen (23) son's life. Sounds good, right?
* Everyone else is kind of playing catch up to him.
* This feels like a low-budget *Law & Order*\-style TV procedural. It's absolutely shot like one. Acted like one. Lots of close-ups. The music. It all screams TV.
* Speaking of that no nudity, no cursing, next to no blood... a few minor icky moments. Again... TV-MA (maybe)
* I'm convinced this was originally conceived as a TV pilot... the kind that a lower-level CBS would have. Is there a lower-level CBS? Maybe a Tubi original procedural.
* There's so many places for MST3K-style jokes I couldn't keep track...
   * Why does this tiny town have a media presence like a small city?
   * When there's no actual case going on, why are all the background cops running around like they're trying to solve something?
   * Why does Josh tell his friend he's leaving and not to tell anyone, then leaves literally next to a press conference with the mayor?
   * Why doesn't the serial killer just tell Josh what's up instead of playing this game?
   * Why is the game so easy? Literally Josh just goes from location to location that's been spelled out.
   * How does this kid killer know everything that's happening? The writer treats him like he's Hannibal Lecter-level brilliant, but he's just an annoying 20-year-old.
   * ADDED: I forgot but someone here reminded me...  this guy Josh is a retiring cop and he recoils in terror when he sees a cut off small body part or body like he's a teenager in a slasher movie. Hilarious.
* Then the movie ends... but it doesn't. It keeps going like the last few minutes of a TV procedural (see previous note).
* There's a slight reveal in this that's so insane and makes so little sense, but I don't want to spoil things. If I did, it would be five more notations of how dumb it is. But it would also have been a better movie if it was just about that insane reveal.

Having said all that... if you find this on Tubi or something, you might like it while you look at your phone.

text:
The Sheep Detectives

Hugh Jackman plays a loving shepherd who reads mystery novels to his flock of sheep every day. What he doesn't know is the sheep actually understand the story, and enjoy figuring out the culprit before the protagonist does. When a murder is committed in their small English town and the police have no clues, the sheep have to take matters into their own hooves to bring the killer to justice.

I came for the talking animals, and left with a charming and emotional mystery film. This is what I call a good family movie, which is something that can be enjoyed by people of all age groups, and not just dumbed down entertainment for the kids. The sheep are cute and fluffy, no doubt about it, but I greatly enjoyed the movie for its decent murder mystery, genuinely funny moments, and tender emotional core. It also has all-around good performance from both the voice actors and the human cast. The Sheep Detectives reminds me of well-thought-out animal movies that I watched as a kid (like Babe or Homeward Bound). Don't skip this sweet movie.
label: review

text:
"Animal Farm" A-List pocket Review (animated)

Well, I read George Orwell's "Animal Farm" book a few decades ago and it has always been a favorite of mine, so when I saw that an animated version had been made, I decided to spend an A-List slot on it.

Anyway, I think most know the story - Orwell uses a barnyard animal takeover of a farm run by humans as an allegory of the communist revolution in Russia - and for the first two thirds or so of "Animal Farm" this is conveyed well enough, if also in a very pedestrian way. The animation is fine, and the big-name voice cast - we get Glenn Close, Seth Rogen, Steve Buscemi and Woody Harrelson, among others -  is fine. But, the last third of the film, "Animal Farm" goes off the rails. And it's not merely that the film deviates from the book. I have no problem with deviations from books, even major ones, that work (see "Jaws" for example), but the deviations in this movie do not work at all. We end up with a big sloppy mess of over the top action scenes that totally blow up the intimate vibe of the farm setting that IMO is crucial to the film. A major fumble by the makers.

C-minus .... I wanted to recommend this movie, but I can't.

PS - during the credits, I was surprised to see that this was distributed by Angel Studios, as I discerned no overt religious messaging. There is the usual "pay it forward" option during those credits.

"Hokum" A-List pocket Review

Well I like horror films and since it was Tuesday and I was itching to see a movie, "Hokum" fit the bill for an A-List slot, especially since I am a fan of Adam Scott, who I still think of as a "Parks and Rec" actor even though he's been in many things since.

Anyway, Scott plays an American author who travels to a remote Irish Inn to scatter his parent's ashes. While there, he hears tails of a witch that allegedly haunts the grounds. It soon becomes apparent that the author is struggling with demons of his own, and after talking to an attractive bartender, attempts to hang himself in his room. Saved by the bartender then finding out she has gone missing, he attempts to unravel the mystery of her disappearance.

"Hokum" worked for me in just about all ways. The Inn is cozy and creepy at the same time. Scott's character is complicated, internally and in how he deals with others. The makers create an atmosphere of creeping dread punctuated by effective shock-terror moments, and we are kept on our toes throughout. I really enjoyed this film.

B+ ... well above average horror film. Much recommended.

text:
"Speed Racer" (2008) A-List pocket Review

Well as a kid growing up in the 1970s, the Japenese anime "Speed Racer" was my favorite cartoon. And we had so many fun, cool cartoons to watch back then, but "Speed" was the best. Heck when I was 9, Trixie was my first crush, LOL. So when the Wachowski Brothers unleashed this live-action film on us back in 2008, I was eager to see it. But I was underwhelmed when I did, so seeing that it has been re-released for a limited time, and I that I had not seen it since then,  I decided to use an A-List slot to find out if the passage of 18 years (!!) has changed my view of it.

Anyway, I think I liked "Speed Racer" a bit more than I did at the end of the GW Bush administration. I now appreciate that the casting is perfect. Susan Sarandon as Mom, John Goodman as Pops, cupcake Cristina Ricci as Trixie, and failed-to-launch Emile Hirsch as Speed are all very good - they look and act the parts very well. Only Matt Fox as Racer X doesn't really fit. And the WBs were obvious fans, they sneak in a lot of the classic references - the Mammoth Car, the GRX, Snake Oiler - little tidbits from the anime abound. 

That said though, the film still has major weaknesses. The two being a basic plot that supports say a 95 minute film not the 135 minute chore this movie is. And, the over-the-top stylization and rainbow blasts of color that dominate the film at every turn are hard on the eyes from the git, and just never let up. It's like the shaky-cam usage in those circa-2010 action movies that gave us such a headache. So overall, this film was just tough to get through, in the end I felt like I had endured it more than enjoyed it.

C-minus ... wish I could rate it higher, but for fanatical fans only.
label: review

"Broken Bird" A-List pocket Review

Well, it was the day before my birthday and I was looking for a movie to see. I noticed that "Broken Bird" had been lingering for the past week or so and had a short running time, so I decided to see it.

Anyway, "Broken Bird" is a creepy psychological horror film. Sybil is a mortician assistant and aspiring poet who lives a lonely inward life. she becomes morbidly fascinated with the bodies she is entrusted to embalm. From this basic premise, all kinds of weird things happen, involving strange deaths and a similarly distressed police detective.

I really likes this movie. Rebecca Calder is excellent as Sybil, she just creeps along weirdly throughout the movie, and as her mental state devolves, the movie slow burns with weirdness and tension. The director does a great job of weaving storylines together, and the payoffs are excellent and well earned. One of the best movies I've seen this year.

B+ .... well above average psychological thriller. Much recommended, see while you can.

Desert Warrior mini review... beautiful boring

I'm proud I got through it...  the theater was empty so I was able to check the time without bothering anyone. I imagine very few of you caught this.

Big plus... It's very beautifully shot like gorgeous. Director of Rise of the Planet of the Apes.

It's very well acted. Everyone is giving it their all.

The story could have been great, it has elements of Ghandi and Braveheart and Gladiator...  someone should have been able to whip up a fun historical epic but this just isn't it.

I think they were so intent on it being understandable for international audiences and trying to be as accurate as possible with that in mind, they missed the boat on both.

They bring up names of tribes like we're supposed to know what it means... cultural things happen without setting them up. It's a series of nice scenes and shots. You get the overall arc of the story... it's just the why was confusing a bit.

The big issue is it's just dull and waiting around until the last act. The last act is quite good but you're not really invested too much. And even then you get confused with which tribe is which...  which flank is who.

But this in no way is like the worst movie ever made...  many nice things about it. Just falls flat in telling the story.

Plus the title is awful. So generic. And really has nothing to do with what it's actually about.

text:
"Mile End Kicks" A-List pocket Review

Well I felt like a movie on Wednesday afternoon, and saw that "Mile End Kicks" was playing. This looked like one of those artsty-quirky-hipster kind of things that, despite not being arsty or quirky or hipstery myself, I tend to enjoy. So off to AMC I went.

Anyway, "Mile End Kicks" is a slice of life coming of age kind of thing. Set in Montreal's Mile End neighborhood circa 2011, An early-twenties-something girl, struggling to launch but with a love of "Indie" rock music, leaves her dullish life in Toronto for Montreal, hoping to write a book on Alanis Morrissette and to report on the city's thriving indie-rock scene of the time. Moving in with a friend who is already settled there, she ends up struggling and forging through her journalistic work, her book writing, financial crunches, and hooking up with various rock band members. This goes on for about 110 minutes of youthful pain and joy and discovery.

I mean, I kind of liked this movie. It \*is\* very artsy/quirky/hippy, and the makers and cast do a good job of evoking the time and place (I happened to spend time in Montreal in 2010-2011 and remember the scene), as well as the familiar struggles of being 20ish and trying to launch. The movie was clearly made by someone with a passion for all these things so you are drawn in by it.  Still, it is perhaps 20 or so minutes long, there are scenes that seem repetitive. But this is a minor thing, overall.

B ... decent indie/quirky/artsy movie about an indie/quirky/artsty music scene 15 years ago.
label: review

"Normal" A-List pocket Review

Well I'm a big fan of Bob Odenkirk, his "Breaking Bad" and "Better Call Saul" character is IMO one of the best we've seen on TV the past 20 years, so I have made a habit of watching his movies. And when I saw he was starring in "Normal", that was enough to draw me to the theater.

Anyway, Odenkirk stars as Ulysses, a Sheriff-for-hire who fills in temporarily when a town is between full time sheriffs and needs a temp. He's hired by Normal, MN to do just this, and when he arrives, the town does indeed seem utterly boring and normal on the surface. But a bank robbery soon reveals that strange doings are happening, involving just about everyone in town, a big pile of cash and gold, as well as the Japenese Yakuza crime organization. Lots and lots and lots of gunfighting ensues. This goes on for about 90 minutes.

Basically, I liked "Normal" while the film was, well, normal, with the sheriff interacting with the local townspeople and fellow law enforcement. Henry Winkler, who will always be The Fonz to me, is good as the mayor, and we get one of the pretty women from Game of Thrones as well. These interactions have a quirky, "Fargo" vibe that worked. But once the fireworks start, the film devolves into just a mass orgy of shooting and killing and over the top disbelief. This bored me, and since the fireworks are about 80% of the movie, it bored me.

C - minus .... recommended for John Wick-type blast away fans only.
label: review

text:
"Ferris Bueller's Day Off" (1986) 40th anniversary A-List pocket Review

Well I was 20 years old in 1986 when "Ferris Bueller" was released, but like "Stand By Me" last month, this is a famous movie - famous among my generation at least - that I had never, ever seen, so my wife convinced me to see it on a hazy warm Friday afternoon. So off to AMC we went.

Anyway, among people over 50, saying you have never seen "Ferris Bueller" is kind of like IDK, if you are 25 right now and have never seen one of the Harry Potter movies. You get astonished looks. Because the film did make a big splash back in the day and has kept its generational resonance for 40 years now. So now I don't have to admit to that among my peers, LOL.

That said, I am not sure why the movie is esteemed. The cast is fine - Matthew Broderick plays a twerpy Chicago-area high school kid who for some unknown reason is beloved by everybody - students, teachers, the community - save for the "evil" principal of his school (Jeffrey Jones), and his sister (Jennifer Grey) who is envious of how glides through life getting away with things. Mia Sara is great as his girlfriend, though her main jobs seem to be to glow lovingly at him and look angelically beautiful, both of which she accomplishes with ease. But the set pieces do not work well for me, I didn't laugh a lot even as I nostalgically enjoyed the mid-80s scenery and culture. Maybe it was a case of "you had to have seen it then".

Overall, FBDO struck me as an amalgam of of other 1980s films. There is a bit of Sean Penn's Jeff Spicoli (Fast Times at Ridgemont High) and Tom Cruise (Risky Business) in Broderick's character. But these were better characters  in much better movies.

C+ .... Recommended only to those for whom it is a cherished part of their childhood/teen years.
label: review

"2die4" A-List Pocket Review

Long time reader, first time pocket review-er.

I saw this because the film producer/director popped into my local subreddit to let us know that the film would be playing at my local AMC (Metreon, for any other bay area folks here!). The central focus is Brazilian driver Felipe Nasr's attempt to win the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

It's the first-ever Brazilian IMAX film and the first-ever IMAX release to use an "anamorphic lens" to make use of the full IMAX 1.43:1 ratio. So that's cool.

It is potentially the most visually stunning movie I've seen. I might put it in between Interstellar 70mm IMAX and the other 70mm IMAX films I've seen at Metreon. The visuals alone make this film worth seeing. There were multiple times where I audibly (quietly - don't worry, I tried to have good etiquette) said "wow" to myself.

The storyline is also unique. They got unparalleled, real-time access to Nasr during one of the most intense sporting events. They follow him through the garage, as he's speaking with his team, throughout the race with a bunch of on-board cameras....as a lifelong racing fan, that *also* made the film worth seeing.

A . . . I'd recommend seeing it if you can. It has a short run (from yesterday until April 20th).

PS - it's only an hour, so you can totally pair this with another movie for a fun double feature.

PPS - at least at Metreon, it started right at the listed showtime, even though the AMC app said the film would start 25-30 minutes after the listed showtime.

PPPS - this review got immediately removed the second I first posted it. Couldn't figure out why. I think it got dinged because of Rule 3's prohibition on all-caps.

"Hunting Matthew Nichols" A-List pocket Review

Well I had a couple of free hours before the final round of the Master's tournament the other day, and "Hunting Matthew Nichols" was playing at noon, and since it looked kind of spooky, and short, I decided to use an A-List slot on it.

Anyway, HMN is one of those Blair Witch inspired found-footage films. Back in 2001, a couple of teenagers were lost in the Vancouver CA area wilderness, and their disappearances was never solved. Now in 2023,  Tara Nichols, played by the fetching Miranda Macdougall, the younger sister of one of the lost boys, decides to investigate by making a documentary film on his disappearance. A camcorder that one of the boys lost is key evidence, and interviews and hikes through the woods on searches follow.

Overall, I liked HMN quite a bit. The acting is smart and on point, as is the path of the investigation. The found footage and interviews provide breadcrumbs that lead in certain directions but not obviously so, so you are kept guessing. And the makers create a building sense of dread, a creeping atmosphere that mirrors the haunting fog of the Canadian wilderness. So the payoffs are good and feel earned.

B .. above average found footage horror/mystery. Recommended.

PS ... there is a mid-credits scene and an end credits stinger.
label: review

text:
Exit 8

Have you ever had a nightmare where you're trapped in a boring, deserted liminal space with no escape? Based on a video game, Exit 8 is a Japanese psychological drama about a man stuck in an unending loop of the same (but not really) subway corridor and has to identify "anomalies" to progress to the exit. 

I enjoyed this movie for its unique concept and stylish directing. It really made me feel like playing a video game. There were some interesting social commentaries at play about how our monotonous lives are no different from being stuck in purgatory. Keep in mind that the movie did get repetitive due to the nature of the premise, and the way the main character kept spelling out every little thing was a bit grating. Overall, it's worth checking out for the concept alone. I don't know if there are any plan to expand, but at the moment Exit 8 is only playing at around 500 theaters. 

Side note: I learned about M. C. Escher and judicial scrivener thanks to the movie.
label: review

"Fantasy Life" A-List pocket Review

Well my wife only sees "people" movies, she has no interest in animated 3D video game films, sci-fi or superhero SFX extravaganzas or horror blood baths, which if you think about it narrows her options down quite a bit these days. But when I found "Fantasy Life" on this week's roster, she watched the trailer and was sold, so off to AMC we went.

Anyway, Writer-Director-lead actor Matt Shear plays a Jewish law school drop out living on the upper west side of Manhattan. When he loses his menial job, his psychiatrist (Judd Hirsch) recommends him as a babysitter to his son's family, a wealthy Jewish clan featuring Amanda Peet and three little girls. Shear integrates himself in to the family well, and becomes kind of a "manny" when the musician dad goes on a three month road tour. Relational stuff happens.

We liked "Fantasy Life" a lot. Shear is basically following in Woody Allen's footsteps here. The film is a slice of life about Jewish anxiety and relations in upper crust New York. While Shear lacks peak Allen's razor wit and comedic genius, the writing is emotionally honest and the set pieces gently humorous and sometimes hearttugging. The story unfold in a believable manner, the acting is spot-on, and the film has a warm heart. And at just about 88 minutes, it does not overstay.

B ... above average slice of life drama-comedy,  handled warmly and gently. Recommended.
label: review

text:
"Stand By Me" (1986) A-List pocket Review

Well continuing my A-List tour of these "anniversary" releases, my wife convinced me to see "Stand By Me", celebrating its 40th anniversary this year. This is one of those well-known movies, at least to people of my generation, that I had never seen before, so while I've never had a particular desire to see it, my wife was convincing so off to AMC we went.

Anyway,  four kids in 1959 Oregon, 12 years old and on the cusp of everything, are close friends who overhear older boys, the town's teenage tough guys, talking about a dead body they have found. The kids decide to go on a walking adventure to find it, and adventures ensue.

"Stand By Me" is a famous movie. I recall it causing a stir when it was released. It was a box office success in 1986, and its soundtrack, filled with 50s doo-wop classics, was a revival hit. It was then and remains regarded by many critics as a classic boys "coming of age" story, and I now see why. The film is engaging start to finish. The cast, including many young actors who would go on to fame, and one, River Phoenix, who would be dead within a few years, is marvelous. Credit to the late Rob Reiner for directing these kids with heart and soul, the chemistry among them is spot-on, and so we quickly come to care about them and their dreams and fears. The short 84  minutes of run time flew by in an instant, and I now see what I have been missing all these years.

text:
"The Mummy Returns" (2001) A-List pocket Review

Well it is hard to believe that is has been a quarter-century since Universal unleashed the sequel to its highly successful 1999 "The Mummy" film on us. Released a few months after the political drama of the Bush-Gore election, and a few months before the horror of 911, "The Mummy Returns" did great box office (I saw it during its original run) as a swashbuckling action-adventure film. So now we get a 25th anniversary release, and I decided to see it via A-List.

Anyway, "The Mummy Returns" has the same strengths and weaknesses as it did back at the dawn of the Millennium. On the plus side, the preternaturally gorgeous Rachel Weisz, still in the full bloom of youth, lights up the screen. Brendan Fraser brings his goofy charm as the Indiana Jones clone, and they have good couple-chemistry. And historically, this is the film debut of The Rock, whose career outside of wrestling failed to launch and was never heard from again (LOL).

But mostly the film remains bad. The main reason is the creators decided to go hog-wild on CGI, so we get a constant blizzard of computer created mummies, massed desert armies, evil Egyptian gods and other sundry creatures, including the Rock's mug on a Scorpion's body. Looking back, we can trace the bad trend of action (and horror) directors assaulting our senses with never-ending waves of creatures to this film. The human characters, who are played by good actors with charisma, are just never allowed to really interact, because the next wave of attacks is right around the corner.

C-minus. Disappointing sequel to "The Mummy". See it for nostalgic reasons only.

text:
"Get On The Bus" (1996) A-List pocket Review

Well it has been almost 30 years since I saw "Get On The Bus" in the theater, and I do not believe I've seen it in any format since. I liked the movie back then, I think it is one of Spike Lee's best. But I was curious as to how an opinion formed during the middle of the Clinton administration would hold up today, so an A-List slot was duly spent. I believe the movie is being shown by AMC as part of a "Black History Month" promotion. 

Anyway, "Get On The Bus" held up ... very well. The film follows a group of black men boarding a bus in Los Angeles to attend the "million man march", an event held by the Nation of Islam in October 1995 in Washington DC. Almost the entire movie takes place on the bus, and consists of interactions among these men, who have different life stories and motivations for wanting to attend.

The movie works because the acting is very good, as is the dialogue. None of the conversations seem forced or hackneyed, and over the course of 120 minutes we learn a lot about each character, and also about the mindsets of some black men in 1990s America. If you are thinking a movie like this will be boring, it was not in the least. I was also surprised at how many of the issues and mindsets exhibited seem to be still relevant, three decades later. 

B+ .... well done social commentary film. Recommended.

PS - trivia: The great Ossie Davis, deceased since 2005, plays an elderly character intent on attending because he regrets having missed MLK's March on Washington in 1963. The actor himself actually did attend the 1963 event, and was  a speaker at it.
label: review

text:
Worst Experience I’ve Ever Had in a Theater.

I started typing this and got increasingly more pissed off about the situation, so I apologize for the rant/length of this post:

I’m usually not one for posting in subreddits, however I keep getting notifications of people discussing their experiences so I figured I’d share mine which happened a couple days ago.

It’s a clickbait title, I won’t lie. There’s been countless movies that I’ve gone to where the theater was in rough shape and people are rude/texting, but it’s a movie, as long as the movie is good, I don’t unusually mind.  I saw Iron Lung this past weekend and movie was lovely, I truly enjoyed every second of it, that is when I could fully focus on it. I’ve been to countless movie theaters in my 26 years of life and have never once seen someone get kicked out of a movie. That changed during my screening of Iron Lung.

I figured that going close to opening, I would be with likeminded people to myself, excited to see Mark’s debut. What I hadn’t counted on, was this movie gaining so much traction that normies started to go see it. There were (at least) three guys sitting behind me, commenting on the movie just about the entire time. If you live in NYC you’ll come to grips with the fact that this happens allllllll the time and unfortunately ya just have to get used to it. The difference in this one was the children were loudly attempting to intentionally “rage bait” the crowd into getting mad at them.

Whenever the movie would hit a lull or a slower point, excitations of “Fat hairy C\*\*\*“ and “thick moist p\*\*\*\*” could be heard from the back of the theater, as well as just general (unfunny) jokes in an attempt to make them the center of the movie going experience.

Eventually someone leaves the theater in an attempt to get someone in there to calm them down. This was met with countless yelling of things like “YOU GO TELL ON US AND WE’LL BEAT YOUR ASS”.

That individual then gets security in the theater where security then walks through the two aisles in front of me (the rowdy group was sitting behind me) with a (quite bright) flashlight, while the movie is playing. Nothing comes of this interruption as the group was not confronted or asked to leave.

Due to this, the group gets more brazen and louder. Comments of “fuck you guys” and “fuck this movie” start raining down on the crowd which got met with quite a few shushes, myself included. Since they were sitting toward the back of the theater and all of (in their eyes) their “antagonizers” were sitting in front of them, that’s when they started throwing small food items.

More people leave to complain about them which leads to the security guard coming back and finally asking them to leave. This did not go well. Since the AMC security person doesn’t have the power or backup to forcibly remove them, the group gets more rowdy. Throwing expletives at the employee, making dangerous threats to him and the crowd, making fun of him relentlessly and continuing to yell about their displeasure for the movie. This came at a very important part of the movie where a lot of plot was just overridden with “f this movie and f all you”.

Eventually, somehow, the security guard gets them to leave. More yelling, a ton more threats, all capped off with one of the individuals tossing his slushie all over the screen virtually ruining the next 45 minutes of the movie.

Due to all this disruption, I think I missed around 3/5ths of the movie. There has to be a better way to handle this type of situation. Like I said, I’ve never really had a “bad” movie going experience so I’m sure this situation is a dime a dozen and it’s not like they can add cops to every single AMC. But these dudes were throwing out threats like it was nothing and with the recent unrest in this country, for a second there, I genuinely thought a gun was about to be pulled.

It just seems unfortunate that there’s one-two security guards for a massive four leveled theater where they have no real power to remove someone from the premises and no real training on how to handle this type of situation. I would hope that the kid throwing the slushie got some sort of penalty but it seems almost impossible to do so in NYC where they can just run into the street and get lost in the crowd.

I’m not sure what a real solution could be and I’m interested to see what people have to say about this/if you’ve had any experiences like this and how the AMC staff handled it there. You can’t use force as I’m sure it would make the situation worse, but the situation in whole seems mismanaged. Especially checking asiles with a flash light during the movie where the disruption most certainly was not.

In general, the concept of “rage baiting” pisses me off. Just be a human being man, you don’t have to intentionally piss someone off or spout bullshit to get a reaction. What happened to genuine conversations! But that’s a rant for another post.

All in all though, Iron Lung, great movie. AMC NYC Lincoln square, rough time.

TLDR: A rowdy group was able to disrupt a movie for a good 3/4 of it, until proper measures were taken to kick them out. Seems like AMC does not have the support needed for their staff to get potentially dangerous and rowdy individuals out of a screening.
